title: An adjunction lifts to fixed pairs when the right exchange is its invertible mate
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, and let $L\dashv R$ have unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ be endofunctors. Use their fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Suppose $e:L G\xrightarrow{\sim}F L$ and $b:R F\xrightarrow{\sim}G R$, where juxtaposition here denotes diagrammatic composition: $L G=G\circ L$ and $R F=F\circ R$. Assume $b$ is the mate of $e^{-1}$ under $L\dashv R$ on both sides [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; in ordinary composition notation its component is
$$ b_M=R(G(\varepsilon_M))\circ R(e^{-1}_{RM})\circ\eta_{FRM}:FRM\longrightarrow RGM. $$
Then the functors
$$ \widetilde L(K,\theta)=(LK,L(\theta)\circ e_K),\qquad \widetilde R(M,\psi)=(RM,R(\psi)\circ b_M) $$
with $L$ and $R$ acting on carrier morphisms are adjoint, $\widetilde L:\mathcal C^F\rightleftarrows\mathcal D^G:\widetilde R$. The unit and counit are morphisms of fixed pairs whose carrier components are exactly $\eta_K$ and $\varepsilon_M$. No equivalence assumption on $F$ or $G$ is needed once the invertible mate $b$ is supplied.

proof.text:
Use ordinary right-to-left composition throughout this proof, so $e_K:GLK\to LFK$ and $b_M:FRM\to RGM$. Put $t_K=L(\theta)\circ e_K$ and $s_M=R(\psi)\circ b_M$. These are isomorphisms, since functors carry an inverse to an inverse. For a fixed-pair map $u:(K,\theta)\to(K',\theta')$, the defining equation in [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] and naturality of $e$ give
$$L(u)\circ t_K=L(u\circ\theta)\circ e_K=L(\theta')\circ L(Fu)\circ e_K=t_{K'}\circ G(Lu).$$
For $v:(M,\psi)\to(M',\psi')$, naturality of $b$ similarly gives
$$R(v)\circ s_M=R(v\circ\psi)\circ b_M=R(\psi')\circ R(Gv)\circ b_M=s_{M'}\circ F(Rv).$$
Thus both prescribed object maps and carrier maps define functors; their identity and composition laws are those of $L$ and $R$.

proof.text:
Write $a=e^{-1}:LF\to GL$. The component formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives the unit-mate identity by the following direct calculation:
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{LK}\circ F(\eta_K)
&=R(G\varepsilon_{LK})\circ R(a_{RLK})\circ\eta_{FRLK}\circ F(\eta_K)\\
&=R(G\varepsilon_{LK}\circ a_{RLK}\circ L(F\eta_K))\circ\eta_{FK}\\
&=R(G\varepsilon_{LK}\circ G(L\eta_K)\circ a_K)\circ\eta_{FK}
=R(a_K)\circ\eta_{FK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second line is naturality of $\eta$ for $F(\eta_K)$, the third is naturality of $a$ for $\eta_K$, and the last uses $\varepsilon_{LK}\circ L(\eta_K)=1_{LK}$. This uses only the given adjunction and the cited component formula, rather than assuming an additional mate-compatibility lemma.

source.place: map_unit_app_comp_str, lines 46–61, with the mate formula expanded

proof.text:
For $(K,\theta)$, the structure of $\widetilde R\widetilde L(K,\theta)$ is $R(t_K)\circ b_{LK}$ by step 1. Step 2, cancellation of $e_K\circ a_K=1_{LFK}$, and naturality of $\eta$ for $\theta:FK\to K$ give
$$R(t_K)\circ b_{LK}\circ F(\eta_K)=R(L\theta)\circ R(e_K)\circ R(a_K)\circ\eta_{FK}=RL(\theta)\circ\eta_{FK}=\eta_K\circ\theta.$$
This is exactly the fixed-pair morphism condition in [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Hence $\eta_K$ is a morphism $(K,\theta)\to\widetilde R\widetilde L(K,\theta)$.

The components in steps 3 and 4 form natural transformations $\widetilde\eta$ and $\widetilde\varepsilon$. Indeed, for a fixed-pair map $u$ the carrier naturality equation is $RL(u)\circ\eta_K=\eta_{K'}\circ u$, and for $v$ it is $v\circ\varepsilon_M=\varepsilon_{M'}\circ LR(v)$; these are the naturality equations of the original unit and counit. Equality of carrier maps implies equality of fixed-pair maps because the forgetful functor is faithful [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. The same faithfulness proves the two lifted triangle identities: their carriers are exactly $\varepsilon_{LK}\circ L(\eta_K)=1_{LK}$ and $R(\varepsilon_M)\circ\eta_{RM}=1_{RM}$.

For fixed pairs $A=(K,\theta)$ and $B=(M,\psi)$ define
$$\widetilde\Phi(f)=\widetilde R(f)\circ\widetilde\eta_A,\qquad \widetilde\Phi^{-1}(g)=\widetilde\varepsilon_B\circ\widetilde L(g).$$
These are morphisms of fixed pairs by steps 1, 3 and 4. On carriers, naturality and the triangle identities from step 5 give
$$\varepsilon_M\circ LR(f)\circ L(\eta_K)=f\circ\varepsilon_{LK}\circ L(\eta_K)=f,$$
$$R(\varepsilon_M)\circ RL(g)\circ\eta_K=R(\varepsilon_M)\circ\eta_{RM}\circ g=g.$$
Faithfulness in [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] makes them inverse on fixed-pair Hom sets. For $u:A'\to A$, $v:B\to B'$, naturality of $\widetilde\eta$ and functoriality give $\widetilde\Phi(f\circ\widetilde L(u))=\widetilde\Phi(f)\circ u$ and $\widetilde\Phi(v\circ f)=\widetilde R(v)\circ\widetilde\Phi(f)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to these natural bijections. Its specified unit is $\widetilde\Phi(1)=\widetilde\eta$ and its counit is $\widetilde\Phi^{-1}(1)=\widetilde\varepsilon$, so their carriers are precisely the original $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. Invertibility of $F$ and $G$ was never used; only the supplied isomorphisms $e,b,\theta,\psi$ were inverted.
